title: Data Log 1: Creating and reading profile cards
lessonSummary: Great! You create dictionaries and read values by their key.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create a dictionary and read from it.
Create a dictionary member with the keys name ("Nova"), role ("Pilot"), rank (4) and energy (120). Print exactly Name: Nova and on the next line Rank: 4 (access with []).
The dictionary member is given. Print the number of entries with len() as Number of properties: 4 and on the next line Role: Pilot.

title: Data Log 2: Changing, adding and removing
lessonSummary: Nice! You change values, add entries and remove them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: change, add, remove.
tasks.codeTemplate:
member = {"name": "Nova", "role": "Pilot", "rank": 4, "energy": 120}
member["rank"] = member["rank"] + 1
member["shield"] = 80
removed = member.pop("energy")
print(f"Rank now: {member['rank']}")
print(f"Removed: {removed}")
print(f"Properties: {len(member)}")

tasks.instruction: The dictionary member is given. Increase rank with += 1 and add the new key shield with the value 80. Print exactly Rank: 5 and on the next line Shield: 80.
The dictionary member is given. Remove the key role with pop() and print the removed value as Removed: Pilot. Then delete the key energy with del and print Properties: 2 (len).

title: Data Log 3: Safe access with get() and in
lessonSummary: Well done! You ask with get() and in instead of risking a KeyError.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: get() with a default value and in.
tasks.codeTemplate:
member = {"name": "Nova", "role": "Pilot", "rank": 4, "energy": 120}
print("Name:", member.get("name"))
print("Shield:", member.get("shield", 0))
print("Present:", "shield" in member)

tasks.instruction: The dictionary member is given (without shield). Fetch the value of shield with get() and default value 0 and print exactly Shield: 0.
The dictionary member is given. Check with in and print exactly rank present: True and on the next line shield present: False.

validation.expected:
rank present: True
shield present: False

title: Data Log 4: Looping through dictionaries
lessonSummary: Great! You walk through a dictionary with keys(), values() and items().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: items() and values().
The dictionary stock is given (Stock: name and amount). With items(), print each entry as Name: Amount on its own line, e.g. Battery: 3.
The dictionary stock is given. Add up all amounts with values() and print exactly Total: 10 and on the next line Kinds: 3 (len).

title: Data Log 5: Tuples
lessonSummary: Nice! You pack values into tuples and unpack them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create, read and unpack a tuple.
tasks.codeTemplate:
part = ("Shield module", 15, "Energy")
print(part)
print("Length:", len(part))
print("First:", part[0])
name, value, kind = part
print(f"Value: {value}")

tasks.instruction: Create the tuple part = ("Shield module", 15, "Energy") and unpack it into name, value and kind. Print exactly Name: Shield module and on the next line Kind: Energy.
Two points are given as tuples. Calculate the distance as the difference of the x values plus the difference of the y values (goal minus start, all positive) and print exactly Distance: 7.

title: Data Log 6: Immutable and catching errors
lessonSummary: Masterful! You catch errors with try/except instead of letting your program crash.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: catch three kinds of errors.
The tuple part is given. In a try block, try to set part[1] = 99, catch the TypeError and print exactly Error: protected.
The dictionary stock is given. In a try block, try to read stock["Warp core"], catch the KeyError and print exactly Not in store: Warp core.
The input text = "ten" is given. In a try block, convert it to number with int(). Catch the ValueError and then set number = 0. Print exactly Number: 0.

title: Data Log 7: Nested structures
lessonSummary: World class! You nest dictionaries, lists and tuples.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: read nested data and filter.
tasks.codeTemplate:
member = {"name": "Nova", "role": "Pilot", "rank": 4, "energy": 120, "equipment": {"tool": "Laser", "suit": "Spacesuit"}}
print(f"Tool: {member['equipment']['tool']}")
crew = [
    {"name": "Nova", "role": "Pilot", "rank": 4, "energy": 120},
    {"name": "Rex", "role": "Engineer", "rank": 6, "energy": 150},
    {"name": "Zara", "role": "Botanist", "rank": 3, "energy": 90},
]
print(f"Count: {len(crew)}")
strong = [e["name"] for e in crew if e["rank"] > 3]
print(f"Strong: {strong}")

tasks.instruction: The list crew with three dictionaries is given. Print exactly Count: 3 and on the next line Last: Zara (name of the last entry, index -1).
The dictionary member contains the sub-entry equipment and is given. Print exactly Tool: Laser and on the next line Suit: Spacesuit.
The list crew is given. With a list comprehension, collect the names of all entries whose rank is greater than 3 into strong and print exactly Strong: ['Nova', 'Rex'].

title: Debug Quest

title: Mission 3: The Station Crew
lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: Searching, counting and averaging across a whole list of profile cards!

title: Extra Challenge 3: The Crew Archive
lessonSummary: The archive stands: searching, counting and a ranking from four profile cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create: Create the list crew with four dictionaries (keys name, role, rank): Nova (Pilot, 4), Rex (Engineer, 6), Zara (Botanist, 3), Kai (Pilot, 5). Print exactly Count: 4.
Step 2 – Search: The list crew is given. Write a function find_crew(items, kind) that returns the names with this role. Print exactly Pilot: 2 and on the next line Engineer: 1 (number of hits).

Step 3 – Ranking: The list crew is given. Collect all rank values, sort them in descending order and find the name with the highest value. Print exactly Best: Rex and on the next line Ranking: [6, 5, 4, 3].

title: Extra Challenge 4: The Great Data Archive
lessonSummary: The great review is done: functions, lists and randomness from weeks 5 to 7 – now with dictionaries!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Function with return (week 5): Write create_member(name, kind, level) that returns a dictionary with the keys name, role, rank. Call it with ("Nova", "Pilot", 4) and print exactly Created: Nova and on the next line Rank: 4.

Step 2 – List of dictionaries (week 5/6): Write create_mission(name, difficulty) that returns a dictionary with name, difficulty and status "open". Create the list missions and add three Mission entries with append() (Locate the signal / 1, Launch the probe / 2, Repair the hull / 3). Print exactly Mission count: 3 and on the next line Status: open (status of the first one).
Step 3 – Find the largest value (week 6): The dictionary prices (name → price) is given. Find the most expensive item with a loop and print exactly Most expensive item: Battery (30).
Step 4 – Counting with a dictionary: In word = "spacestation", count how often each letter occurs. Use counter = {} and counter[c] = counter.get(c, 0) + 1. Print exactly a: 2.
Step 5 – Randomness (week 7): The dictionary stock is given. With random.choice(list(stock.keys())), draw a name into drawn and print exactly Drawn valid: True (drawn in stock).

Step 6 – Catch errors (week 5/8): The dictionary stock is given. Write amount_of(name) that returns the amount – or 0 if the name is missing (try/except KeyError). Print exactly Battery: 3 and on the next line Warp core: 0.
